Rights, Responsibilities & the American Community
🗽 What Is Citizenship?
A citizen is a member of a community, state, or country who has both RIGHTS and RESPONSIBILITIES. Rights are the basic freedoms and protections given to people by law. Responsibilities are the duties and obligations people must do to respect the rights of others and keep society safe and fair.
⚖️  Rights of Citizens
Freedom of speech & religion
Right to vote (age 18+)
Right to a fair trial
Right to an education
📋  Responsibilities
Obey laws
Pay taxes
Jury duty
Vote & participate How Do You Become a U.S. Citizen?
🍼  Birth
Born in the United States
Born abroad to at least one U.S. citizen parent
📝  Naturalization
Live in U.S. for 5+ years as a legal resident
Pass a civics test (100 questions)
Take the Oath of Allegiance
Key Vocab: Naturalization – the legal process by which a non-citizen becomes a citizen. ✅  Check for Understanding

How the U.S. Government Works for Its Citizens
🏛️ The Three Branches of Government
The U.S. Constitution created THREE branches to share power and prevent any one group from having too much control.
📜
Legislative
Makes the Laws
Congress (Senate + House)
535 total members
Senate: 100 senators (2 per state)
House: 435 representatives
🏛️
Executive
Carries Out Laws
President & Cabinet
President is Commander-in-Chief
Serves 4-year terms
Signs or vetoes bills
⚖️
Judicial
Interprets Laws
Supreme Court & Federal Courts
9 Supreme Court Justices
Serve for life
Decides if laws are constitutional Checks & Balances
Checks and balances make sure no single branch has too much power. Each branch can limit the others!
Legislative → Executive
Can override a presidential veto with ⅔ vote
Executive → Legislative
President can veto (reject) bills passed by Congress
Judicial → Executive
Courts can declare presidential actions unconstitutional
Judicial → Legislative
Courts can strike down laws that violate the Constitution
Executive → Judicial
President appoints Supreme Court justices
Legislative → Judicial
Senate confirms or rejects judicial nominees ✅  Check for Understanding
Which branch of government is responsible for MAKING laws?
A.  Executive Branch (President)
B.  Judicial Branch (Courts)
C.  Legislative Branch (Congress)
D.  The Cabinet
★ Correct answer: C Levels of Government
Government exists at three levels — each with different roles and responsibilities.
🇺🇸
Federal Government
Entire United States
National defense & military
Foreign policy & treaties
Printing money
Immigration laws
🏛️
State Government
Each individual state
Public schools
Driver's licenses
State roads & highways
State courts
🏘️
Local Government
Cities, counties & towns
Local police & fire dept.
Trash collection
Local parks
Building permits ✅  Check for Understanding
Which level of government is responsible for printing money and national defense?
A.  Local Government
B.  State Government
C.  Federal Government
D.  City Government
★ Correct answer: C The Constitution & Bill of Rights
📜  The U.S. Constitution
Written in 1787 in Philadelphia
The supreme law of the United States
Sets up the structure of government
Protects the rights of citizens
Has been amended 27 times
Begins with 'We the People...'
⚖️  The Bill of Rights
First 10 Amendments to the Constitution
Freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition
Right to Bear Arms - People have the rights to own and carry weapons within the law.
No Forced Housing - Soldiers cannot live in your home
Privacy - the government cannot search you or your things without good reason.
Rights of the Accused - You have the right to remain silent
Fair Trial - You have the right to a speedy and fair trial with a lawyer and jury.
Jury in Civil Cases - You have the right to a jury in certain disagreements involving money or property.
Fair Punishment - No cruel or unusual punishment or unreasonable fines and bail.
Other Rights - People have other rights, even if they're not’ specifically listed in the Constitution.
Powers of the State and People - Powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or the people.  ✅  Check for Understanding
The Bill of Rights refers to —
A.  The U.S. tax system
B.  The first 10 amendments to the Constitution
C.  A list of rules for businesses
D.  The rules for becoming president
